gloss: non-slip device; anti-slip material; backup school

definitions.explanation: Something that prevents slipping — a mat, coating, treads, snow chains, or any other anti-slip device or material.

In Japanese school entrance exams, a less competitive school that a student applies to as insurance in case they fail to get into their first choice. A figurative extension of the 'preventing slipping' meaning.

examples.japanese: {階段|かいだん}に{滑|すべ}り{止|ど}めを{付|つ}けた。
examples.english: I attached non-slip strips to the stairs.

examples.japanese: {滑|すべ}り{止|ど}めの{付|つ}いた{靴下|くつした}を{履|は}いた。
examples.english: I put on socks with non-slip grips.

examples.japanese: {雪道|ゆきみち}を{走|はし}るので、タイヤに{滑|すべ}り{止|ど}めを{付|つ}けた。
examples.english: Since I'll be driving on snowy roads, I put anti-skid chains on the tires.

examples.japanese: {滑|すべ}り{止|ど}めの{大学|だいがく}も{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I also applied to a backup university.

examples.japanese: {第一志望|だいいちしぼう}に{落|お}ちて{滑|すべ}り{止|ど}めに{進学|しんがく}した。
examples.english: I didn't get into my first choice, so I enrolled at my backup school.

examples.japanese: {受験生|じゅけんせい}は{第一志望|だいいちしぼう}に{加|くわ}えて{滑|すべ}り{止|ど}めを{二三校|にさんこう}{受|う}けるのが{普通|ふつう}だ。
examples.english: It's normal for exam-takers to apply to two or three backup schools in addition to their first choice.

notes:
Compound of {滑|すべ}る (to slip) + {止|と}める (to stop). Literally 'slip-stop.'

The figurative 'backup school' sense plays on the verb {滑|すべ}る, which in student slang also means 'to fail an exam.' A {滑|すべ}り{止|ど}め school 'stops you from failing.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {滑|すべ}り{止|ど}めを{付|つ}ける: to attach a non-slip device
- {滑|すべ}り{止|ど}めの{靴下|くつした}: non-slip socks
- {滑|すべ}り{止|ど}めの{大学|だいがく}: backup university
- {滑|すべ}り{止|ど}めを{受|う}ける: to apply to a backup school

CULTURAL NOTE:
Due to the highly competitive entrance-exam system, Japanese students typically apply to several schools at different difficulty levels, designating one or more as their {滑|すべ}り{止|ど}め.
